The Pop-up Conversion shop (lead capture games for small brands)
6.8
/10

THE IDEA

Meta cost per action rose 38.1% in one year to $38.19, and Apple Mail Privacy plus iOS 26 Digest View broke email metrics along the way. DTC brands doing under $10M pay $15 to $299 a month for the same spin wheel popup every other store runs (Wheelio alone sits on about 2,613 Shopify stores). It works (merchants report 5% to 14% signup rates), but it looks like everyone else and it caps at the template.

This is a done-for-you branded browser game shipped as a lead magnet. A small studio-in-a-box reskins a proven mini-game mechanic in the brand's art, ties it to a scaling discount, hosts it, and exports every email and phone number to Klaviyo, Postscript, or Attentive. $1,500 to $5,000 per campaign setup, $99 to $299 a month to keep it live. Sold first to the small DTC agencies that already run the brand's paid social and want a service they can white-label.

WHY NOW

Meta CPA up 38% in one year while AI makes custom browser games cheap

The math on paid acquisition got worse fast. Meta average CPM rose 20.1% from 2025 to 2026 and cost per action rose 38.1% from $27.66 to $38.19. Q4 2025 ecommerce CPMs hit all-time highs near $23. DTC brands doing $2M-$20M in revenue cannot outbid Temu and Shein in the auction, so they need cheaper ways to fill the top of the funnel. An email or SMS captured on-site at 10% conversion costs a fraction of a paid lead, and merchants on Wheelio report exactly that lift.

The supply side changed too. Y Combinator said 25% of its Winter 2025 batch shipped codebases that were 95% AI-generated, and Collins named vibe coding its 2025 word of the year. WebGPU shipped across major browsers in September 2025. A custom-branded browser game that used to need a MarketJS license at $2K-$16K plus a developer now takes a solo builder with Claude and Cursor a weekend to reskin. That is the price collapse that makes a $1,500-$5,000 done-for-you campaign work as a business, not a favor.

Unlike broad gamification SaaS (Drimify, Playable) that sells a self-serve builder, and unlike enterprise advergame shops that charge six figures, this is a finished, done-for-you campaign at agency-friendly prices for brands under $10M revenue.

THE VERDICT

Should you build this?

REASONS TO BUILD

Meta CPA rose 38.1% to $38.19 in one year while merchants on Wheelio report 5-14% on-site signup rates, so DTC brands under $10M have a hard math reason to pay for a better popup right now.
Drimify's real 2026 pricing (Starter $226/mo, Growth $801/mo) sits above the $99-$299/mo hosting line, and MarketJS charges $1,999-$15,999 per license with no service layer, so a $1,500-$5,000 done-for-you campaign has a clean gap to sell into.
The agency channel already wants this: RootedAI publicly said clients keep asking for browser games so they built one themselves, which is a warm reseller signal you can hunt one DM at a time.
AI coding agents plus a designer can ship a custom branded mini game in a week, which means one founder can deliver 3-5 campaigns a month at 60-70% gross margin without hiring a game studio.

REASONS TO NOT BUILD

Zero Google search volume on every solution-side term (gamified lead capture, branded games for marketing, gamified popup all at 0/mo) means SEO and paid search are dead channels; the whole growth motion is manual DMs and agency intros for years.
Brands may run one game, take the lift, and cancel, collapsing the monthly line into a per-campaign services business with rough gross margins; the seasonal retainer that fights this is unproven.
Drimify or Optimove can bolt on a productized done-for-you tier in 90 days since they already own the tech; the moat is agency relationships and turnaround speed, not code, so a well-funded incumbent could compress the price band overnight.
The buyer is small DTC brands under $10M revenue, a segment that churns hard in downturns and negotiates every invoice; scaling past $500K ARR means either climbing to bigger brands (where Playable and Optimove already live) or grinding agency-by-agency for years.

Not a game studio, not an ML engineer. A creative operator who can sell the pilot on a Loom video and deliver it without hiring. 6.8

THE IDEA

Meta cost per action rose 38.1% in one year to $38.19, and Apple Mail Privacy plus iOS 26 Digest View broke email metrics along the way. DTC brands doing under $10M pay $15 to $299 a month for the same spin wheel popup every other store runs (Wheelio alone sits on about 2,613 Shopify stores). It works (merchants report 5% to 14% signup rates), but it looks like everyone else and it caps at the template.

This is a done-for-you branded browser game shipped as a lead magnet. A small studio-in-a-box reskins a proven mini-game mechanic in the brand's art, ties it to a scaling discount, hosts it, and exports every email and phone number to Klaviyo, Postscript, or Attentive. $1,500 to $5,000 per campaign setup, $99 to $299 a month to keep it live. Sold first to the small DTC agencies that already run the brand's paid social and want a service they can white-label.

WHY NOW

Meta CPA up 38% in one year while AI makes custom browser games cheap

The math on paid acquisition got worse fast. Meta average CPM rose 20.1% from 2025 to 2026 and cost per action rose 38.1% from $27.66 to $38.19. Q4 2025 ecommerce CPMs hit all-time highs near $23. DTC brands doing $2M-$20M in revenue cannot outbid Temu and Shein in the auction, so they need cheaper ways to fill the top of the funnel. An email or SMS captured on-site at 10% conversion costs a fraction of a paid lead, and merchants on Wheelio report exactly that lift.

The supply side changed too. Y Combinator said 25% of its Winter 2025 batch shipped codebases that were 95% AI-generated, and Collins named vibe coding its 2025 word of the year. WebGPU shipped across major browsers in September 2025. A custom-branded browser game that used to need a MarketJS license at $2K-$16K plus a developer now takes a solo builder with Claude and Cursor a weekend to reskin. That is the price collapse that makes a $1,500-$5,000 done-for-you campaign work as a business, not a favor.

THE VERDICT

Should you build this?

REASONS TO BUILD

Meta CPA rose 38.1% to $38.19 in one year while merchants on Wheelio report 5-14% on-site signup rates, so DTC brands under $10M have a hard math reason to pay for a better popup right now.
Drimify's real 2026 pricing (Starter $226/mo, Growth $801/mo) sits above the $99-$299/mo hosting line, and MarketJS charges $1,999-$15,999 per license with no service layer, so a $1,500-$5,000 done-for-you campaign has a clean gap to sell into.
The agency channel already wants this: RootedAI publicly said clients keep asking for browser games so they built one themselves, which is a warm reseller signal you can hunt one DM at a time.
AI coding agents plus a designer can ship a custom branded mini game in a week, which means one founder can deliver 3-5 campaigns a month at 60-70% gross margin without hiring a game studio.

REASONS TO NOT BUILD

Zero Google search volume on every solution-side term (gamified lead capture, branded games for marketing, gamified popup all at 0/mo) means SEO and paid search are dead channels; the whole growth motion is manual DMs and agency intros for years.
Brands may run one game, take the lift, and cancel, collapsing the monthly line into a per-campaign services business with rough gross margins; the seasonal retainer that fights this is unproven.
Drimify or Optimove can bolt on a productized done-for-you tier in 90 days since they already own the tech; the moat is agency relationships and turnaround speed, not code, so a well-funded incumbent could compress the price band overnight.
The buyer is small DTC brands under $10M revenue, a segment that churns hard in downturns and negotiates every invoice; scaling past $500K ARR means either climbing to bigger brands (where Playable and Optimove already live) or grinding agency-by-agency for years.
